sources.entry: biopython - Biopython is a set of freely available tools for biological computation.

summary.one_liner: Biopython is a set of freely available Python tools for computational molecular biology and bioinformatics, maintained by an international volunteer project.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Biopython as an international association of developers producing free Python tools for computational molecular biology. The package is installable with pip and ships pre-compiled wheels for Linux, macOS and Windows. Optional extras add plotting and graph support for phylogenetic trees (Bio.Phylo), graphics output (Bio.Graphics), and PostgreSQL or MySQL database access through BioSQL. The README names modules such as Bio.SeqIO, Bio.Blast, Bio.Phylo, Bio.Graphics and Bio.DocSQL. Full documentation is a Sphinx-generated Tutorial and Cookbook plus API docs. Source code is organized into Bio/, BioSQL/, Doc/, Scripts/ and Tests/ directories.
use_cases: parse sequence file formats like GenBank or FASTA
run BLAST result parsing in Python
store biological sequence data in a BioSQL database
bioinformatics scripting and computational biology research
notable: Pre-compiled binary wheels on PyPI so pip install does not need a compiler
Bio.Phylo for phylogenetic tree handling and plotting
BioSQL integration for PostgreSQL and MySQL databases
caveats: Building from source needs a C compiler and Python development headers; Windows needs Visual Studio Build Tools
Some tests need an internet connection and can fail from network issues; use --offline to skip them
Experimental modules may change between releases
